Subject: Sizing follow-up: latency & burst profile for Olive Health pilot

Hi Samir — thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can finalize the pilot sizing: 

Summary (from call):
- Pilot scope: real-time triage assistant for nursing intake, ~3–4 step prompts per session, optional streaming tokens for partial answers.
- Target UX SLO: 95th perc end-to-end latency <= 400 ms for non-streaming calls; streaming first-token <= 120 ms where enabled.
- Expected steady-state: ~5 sessions/minute during business hours (US PST) for initial roll. Peak bursts driven by morning shift overlap and discharge windows.

Questions for you (please reply inline):
1) Can you confirm average tokens per request? You mentioned ~350 tokens average but that included retrieval text; what's the model-only token delta?
2) Peak burst estimate — you said "spikey mornings" — can you quantify peak QPS in those 5–10 minute windows?
3) Any hard constraints on concurrent streaming connections (e.g., websocket limit)?

Preliminary Redwood sizing assumptions we used in the call (we'll refine after your answers):
- Baseline QPS steady: 0.08 QPS (~5 requests/min)
- Peak crest (rolling 2–5m window): 8 QPS (100x delta for worst-case pilot) — please sanity-check this number
- Avg tokens per response used for cost math: 450 tokens (generation + context)
- Desired safety margin: 1.5x over your peak for canary phase

I've attached the token profile CSV we sketched and a draft SLO matrix for your review. Next steps from Redwood: once you confirm tokens/QPS we will produce a short capacity playbook with recommended instance counts, batching settings, and streaming concurrency knobs.

Thanks — laura

--

Thanks Laura — good recap. Answering inline below.

> 1) average tokens per request?
We looked at historical transcripts: average total tokens (context + response) is ~420. Model generation portion averages 260 tokens; the rest is context/metadata. For safety, plan with 300 tokens generation.

> 2) Peak burst estimate?
Peak observed in a 7-minute window was ~34 requests, so roughly 0.08 -> 0.81 QPS in that crest historically. However, for pilot we may see amplified load during onboarding (support bot + triage) — the business wants to plan to handle up to 6 QPS for short bursts (~10 min).

> 3) concurrent streaming connections
Our infra team caps websocket connections per service at 200 concurrently for now. For the pilot we expect <30 concurrent streaming sessions in production, but we can sustain bursts to 120 for a few minutes.

I'll upload a short CSV from our telemetry next; attaching a sanitized sample. Let me know if you want more granular per-hour heatmaps.

Samir

Thanks for the numbers, Samir — that helps. A few technical follow-ups / proposals from the inference side to keep latency under the SLO while controlling cost: 

Assumptions I've used for a draft sizing exercise:
- Steady QPS: 0.08 QPS (5 req/min)
- Planning peak: 6 QPS sustained for up to 10 minutes during onboarding events; historical crests 0.8 QPS
- Model cost assumptions: 300 gen tokens average, 50 prefill tokens (context trimmed) -> 350 tokens per request for perf math

Sizing proposals / configuration suggestions:
- Streaming: enable streaming for UX-critical flows only (first-token path). Configure a small dedicated router pool with lower-batch/low-latency settings to keep first-token <=120ms. That pool should be autoscaled based on concurrent streams, target 40 concurrent streams headroom.
- Batch sizing: for non-streaming flows we recommend target batch window 10–15 ms with a max batch size tuned for 512 tokens sequence. This balances throughput and tail latency for your steady-state.
- Prefix/KV caching: heavy reuse expected in triage prompts — enable prefix caching and a 30-minute KV TTL to cut gen tokens in half for common templates.
- Fallback model: configure a smaller quantized variant (8-bit) as a fallback for overload to preserve availability, with graceful quality degradation alerts to your SREs.

Preliminary capacity estimate (very rough):
- Baseline (steady): single small instance cluster (n1) with autoscaling policy -> handles 0.08 QPS comfortably; we'd plan 1 dedicated slot for pilot.
- Burst buffer: reserve 2 additional mid-sized inference instances to hit 6 QPS for 10 minutes (1.5x safety).
- Observability hooks: per-request token & latency tracing, and an alert when model-variant fallback occurs >1% of requests.

If that looks reasonable I'll convert this into a short playbook with exact instance types, GPU counts, and expected token cost per hour. Samir — can you confirm whether you want streaming enabled for the whole pilot or just selected flows? Also can you attach the sanitized CSV you referenced so I can align our token-profile assumptions?

— Rishi
